package_info.package_manager: N/A (custom Windows malware, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.package_versions: Current version as used by LuoYu APT
package_info.why_malicious: WinDealer is an information stealer malware deployed by the LuoYu APT group. It is delivered through automatic updates of legitimate applications and enables attackers to search and transmit data from infected Windows systems, install backdoors for persistence, manipulate files, propagate, and execute arbitrary commands. Its primary purpose is unauthorized data exfiltration and system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (post-compromise, after malware installation via fake update)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into legitimate application process or dropped as a separate executable

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker-controlled code searches for sensitive files, collects them, and transmits data to a remote C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C++ (typical for Windows malware, exact language not specified)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates files and directories, collects sensitive data, and sends it to a remote command-and-control server via HTTP/S, enabling data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated searching and exfiltration of user/system data to an external server is a hallmark of infostealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software updates should not search for or transmit user data to unknown remote servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise backup or remote support tools may transmit data, but only to trusted, documented endpoints and with user consent.
key_indicators: Network communication to attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure

execution_context.file_location: Injected into legitimate application process or as a persistent service

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malware installs a backdoor, allowing remote command execution and persistence.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C++ (typical for Windows malware, exact language not specified)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes a persistent backdoor by registering itself as a service or modifying autostart entries, then listens for remote commands from the attacker, enabling arbitrary command execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Installing a backdoor and enabling remote command execution is a core malicious activity, providing attackers with ongoing control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not create unauthorized persistence mechanisms or allow remote command execution without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools (RATs) may have similar features, but are used with explicit consent and proper security controls.
key_indicators: Listening for and executing remote commands

execution_context.file_location: Injected into legitimate application process or as a separate module

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malware manipulates files and propagates to other systems.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C++ (typical for Windows malware, exact language not specified)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code manipulates files (e.g., modifying, deleting, or creating files) and attempts to propagate itself to other systems on the network, enabling lateral movement.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unauthorized file manipulation and self-propagation are classic malware behaviors, used to spread infection and maintain control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software updates should not modify unrelated files or attempt to spread to other systems.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise deployment tools may propagate updates, but only with proper authentication and user awareness.

attack_chain.action: Malware is delivered via automatic updates of legitimate applications, resulting in initial infection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious payload on the victim system

attack_chain.action: Malware searches for and collects sensitive data from the infected system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of data to attacker-controlled infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Malware establishes persistence and backdoor access for ongoing control.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can issue remote commands and maintain access

attack_chain.action: Malware manipulates files and attempts to propagate to other systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential lateral movement and further compromise

behavioral_signatures: Automated file enumeration and exfiltration to unknown remote servers
Creation of unauthorized persistence mechanisms (e.g., new services, autostart entries)
Remote command execution via backdoor communication
Propagation attempts to other systems on the network
file_indicators: Unexpected executables or DLLs in application update directories
New or modified autostart registry entries or scheduled tasks
Files with anomalous names or locations associated with known legitimate applications
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure
Unusual HTTP/S traffic patterns following application updates
Beaconing behavior to dynamic or previously unseen domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected file enumeration and exfiltration activity following application updates, creation of new persistence mechanisms, and outbound connections to suspicious or previously unknown domains. Correlate process creation events with update processes to identify injected or dropped malware components. Use behavioral analysis to detect remote command execution and lateral movement attempts.
